chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has a female slave, and his son has sexual intercourse with her before the grandfather (father) has intercourse with her, or a man commits fornication with a woman, is it permissible for his son to marry her? He said: No. That is only if the father married her and had intercourse with her, then his son committed fornication with her, it would not harm him, because the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible. And similarly with the female slave.
ai.seo_question: Does a father's fornication with a woman prevent his son from marrying her?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a father's fornication (zina) with a woman does not create a permanent impediment (illat) preventing his son from marrying her, distinguishing it from the stricter rules of consanguinity. This ruling exemplifies the Shia juristic principle that 'the forbidden act does not invalidate the permissible relationship' (al-haram la yufsidu al-halal), emphasizing that zina is a sin but not a structural barrier to marriage. The text also extends this logic to the case of a son having sexual relations with a slave girl before his father, reinforcing the consistency of this legal maxim.
